description: The plot illustrates how the maximum activation value varies across transformer layers for four signals (attention output, attention residual, feed-forward output, and feed-forward residual). The x-axis is labeled “Layer,” uses a linear scale, and spans approximately layers 0 to 23 with numeric ticks shown at 5-layer intervals (5, 10, 15, 20). The y-axis is labeled “Max Activation Value,” uses a linear scale, and ranges from about 0 up to about 1600 with evenly spaced tick labels in increments of roughly 200. Four lines are shown: a blue dashed line (attn_output) that stays near 0 through the early layers and then rises gradually in the mid-to-late layers, reaching roughly the 500–600 range by around layer 20 and ending near the upper hundreds by the final layers; an orange dotted line (attn_residual) that jumps sharply from near 0 in the early layers to around 1500 by roughly layer 4–5, remains near the top of the axis (around 1500–1600) across most middle layers, and then drops steeply near the last few layers to end around the high hundreds; a green dash-dot line (ffn_output) that rises sharply to around 1500 by roughly layer 4–5, drops down to a few hundred around layer 6, stays in the low hundreds through much of the middle layers, then increases again in the late layers to around the 500–600 range and ends near the upper hundreds; and a red solid line (ffn_residual) that similarly jumps from near 0 to around 1500 by about layer 4–5, stays near the top (around 1500–1600) through most layers, and then declines sharply near the end, with a visible dip to around ~1000 shortly before the final layers and finishing around the high hundreds.
